knowledge:
- key_parameters: prop=Proportion of cells to randomly sample to start neighbourhood definition (usually 0.1-0.2 for <30k cells, 0.05 for larger datasets) ;; k=Number of nearest neighbors for graph building and refinement (average neighbourhood size should ideally be > 5 * N_samples) ;; d=Number of reduced dimensions (PCs) to use for graph building and refinement ;; refined=Logical indicating whether to use the sampling refinement algorithm (default and recommended TRUE) ;; design=Formula specifying the experimental design (e.g., ~ Condition or ~ sequencing.batch + stage or ~ adjmfc.time + (1|tenx_lane) for GLMM) ;; model.contrasts=Character vector specifying contrasts for multi-group comparisons (e.g., "Age1wk - Age4wk") ;; glmm.solver=Solver for GLMM parameter estimation ("Fisher", "HE", or "HE-NNLS"; "Fisher" is recommended if well-conditioned) ;; REML=Logical, use restricted maximum likelihood for GLMM (recommend TRUE)
- alternatives: Discrete cell clustering (traditional DA testing is done on discrete clusters, but Milo uses overlapping graph neighbourhoods to avoid arbitrary clustering boundaries) ;; BBKNN (graph-based batch correction can be used, but forces random sampling instead of refined sampling, leading to suboptimal DA results) ;; GLM vs GLMM (GLM is faster and standard; GLMM is preferred when there are dependencies between observations, e.g., multiple time points/organs from the same individual, genetic ancestry, family structures, and sample size is large, at least 50 observations)
- when_to_use: When analyzing complex single-cell datasets generated from replicated multi-condition experiments to detect changes in composition (differential abundance) across continuous cell states or trajectories without relying on discrete clustering.
- pitfalls: Low neighbourhood size (if the average neighbourhood size is too small, e.g., < 5 * N_samples, statistical power is reduced; increase k or prop) ;; Batch correction with graph-only tools (like BBKNN forces random sampling instead of refined sampling, leading to suboptimal DA results) ;; GLMM convergence issues (sparse neighbourhood counts can cause GLMM parameter estimation to fail or not converge; use checkSeparation to identify and exclude neighbourhoods with perfect separation) ;; GLMM sample size (do not use GLMM with fewer than 50 observations) ;; Contrasts syntax (must use ~ 0 + Variable in the design to get separate columns for each level when using contrasts)

workflows.name: standard_da_glm
workflows.intent: Perform standard differential abundance testing using a Negative Binomial GLM, followed by neighbourhood annotation, grouping, and marker gene identification.
input: embryo_data (SingleCellExperiment object containing single-cell counts and reduced dimensions)
embryo_design (data.frame matching samples to experimental conditions and technical covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Create Milo object ;; 2. Build KNN graph ;; 3. Define representative neighbourhoods ;; 4. Count cells in neighbourhoods ;; 5. Compute neighbourhood connectivity (distances) ;; 6. Test for differential abundance ;; 7. Annotate and group neighbourhoods ;; 8. Find marker genes for neighbourhood groups ;; 9. Perform differential expression within a group
workflows.code:
embryo_milo <- Milo(embryo_data)
embryo_milo <- buildGraph(embryo_milo, k = 30, d = 30, reduced.dim = "pca.corrected")
embryo_milo <- makeNhoods(embryo_milo, prop = 0.1, k = 30, d=30, refined = TRUE, reduced_dims = "pca.corrected")
plotNhoodSizeHist(embryo_milo)
embryo_milo <- countCells(embryo_milo, meta.data = as.data.frame(colData(embryo_milo)), sample="sample")
embryo_milo <- calcNhoodDistance(embryo_milo, d=30, reduced.dim = "pca.corrected")
da_results <- testNhoods(embryo_milo, design = ~ sequencing.batch + stage, design.df = embryo_design, reduced.dim="pca.corrected")
embryo_milo <- buildNhoodGraph(embryo_milo)
da_results <- annotateNhoods(embryo_milo, da_results, coldata_col = "celltype")
da_results <- groupNhoods(embryo_milo, da_results, max.lfc.delta = 10, overlap=1)
nhood_markers <- findNhoodGroupMarkers(embryo_milo, da_results, subset.row = hvgs, aggregate.samples = TRUE, sample_col = "sample")
dge_6 <- testDiffExp(embryo_milo, da_results, design = ~ stage, meta.data = data.frame(colData(embryo_milo)), subset.row = rownames(embryo_milo)[1:5], subset.nhoods=da_results$NhoodGroup=="6")

workflows.name: da_glmm_random_effects
workflows.intent: Perform differential abundance testing using a Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) to account for random effects and dependencies between observations.
input: pbmc.sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing single-cell counts and reduced dimensions)
pbmc.design (data.frame matching samples to fixed and random effect covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Create Milo object ;; 2. Build KNN graph ;; 3. Define representative neighbourhoods ;; 4. Count cells in neighbourhoods ;; 5. Check for perfect separation ;; 6. Test for differential abundance using GLMM
workflows.code:
pbmc.milo <- Milo(pbmc.sce)
reducedDim(pbmc.milo, "UMAP") <- reducedDim(pbmc.sce, "UMAP")
pbmc.milo <- buildGraph(pbmc.milo, k = 60, d = 30)
pbmc.milo <- makeNhoods(pbmc.milo, prop = 0.05, k = 60, d=30, refined = TRUE, refinement_scheme="graph")
pbmc.milo <- countCells(pbmc.milo, meta.data = data.frame(colData(pbmc.milo)), samples="ObsID")
which(checkSeparation(pbmc.milo, design.df=pbmc.design, condition="adjmfc.time", min.val=10))
da_results <- testNhoods(pbmc.milo, design = ~ adjmfc.time + (1|tenx_lane), design.df = pbmc.design, fdr.weighting="graph-overlap", glmm.solver="Fisher", REML=TRUE, norm.method="TMM", BPPARAM = bpparam, fail.on.error=FALSE)

workflows.name: da_contrasts
workflows.intent: Perform differential abundance testing using contrasts to compare specific groups in multi-group experimental designs.
input: thy.sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing single-cell counts and reduced dimensions)
thy.design (data.frame matching samples to multi-level group covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Create Milo object ;; 2. Build KNN graph ;; 3. Define representative neighbourhoods ;; 4. Count cells in neighbourhoods ;; 5. Test for differential abundance using specified contrasts
workflows.code:
thy.milo <- Milo(thy.sce)
reducedDim(thy.milo, "UMAP") <- reducedDim(thy.sce, "UMAP")
thy.milo <- buildGraph(thy.milo, k = 11, d = 40)
thy.milo <- makeNhoods(thy.milo, prop = 0.2, k = 11, d=40, refined = TRUE, refinement_scheme="graph")
thy.milo <- countCells(thy.milo, meta.data = data.frame(colData(thy.milo)), samples="Sample")
da_results <- testNhoods(thy.milo, design = ~ 0 + Age, design.df = thy.design, model.contrasts = contrast.1, fdr.weighting="graph-overlap", norm.method="TMM")
